items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: D'Hellemes was a good solid bass player who preferred to play trombone. He was also a very agreable fellow and we began to be good friends although I did not speak French and he didn't speak English. The first date with Chit and Eugene was recorded for Ultraphone.

ctx.x: It was a beautiful day when we arrived in Paris and Freddie had rooms for us at a hotel called Eden on rue Pigalle. Later, after we had arranged things in our room, Freddie took us to the cafe Lizieur, a place that I had known when I came to Paris in 1933 and lived in the hotel above. We met the drummer that was engaged to play with Freddie's group. His name was William Diemar. I think that Diemar came to Europe in 1927 with a group from Buffalo.

After rehearsing for one week, we opened at the Villa d'Este on rue Areene-Housaaye near the Arc de Triomphe and the great Avenue des Champs Elysees. The pianist was French by the name of Jean Ferrier, the bass was Eugene D'Hellemes. The guitarist was from America and his name was Oscar Aleman.

Back in the U.S.A. I never played a matinee at the Savoy except on Sundays, National holidays and very special events. At the Roseland and Arcadia, I played them every Thursday, Saturday, Sunday and holidays.
